beats.intro: Chapter fifty-four. [[sub]]Some trinomials, like x squared plus five x plus six, are the product of two binomials. Here's how to find them.
beats.tiles: Build x squared plus five x plus six with algebra tiles: [[sq]]one x squared, [[xs]]five x strips, [[ones]]and six unit squares. [[try]]Factoring means arranging all of them into one rectangle. [[corner]]Put the big square in the corner, [[side]]the x strips along two sides, [[fill]]and the ones fill the corner that's left. [[dims]]The rectangle is x plus two tall and x plus three wide. [[ans]]So x squared plus five x plus six equals x plus two, times x plus three.
beats.why: Why those numbers? [[foil]]Multiply x plus d by x plus e with FOIL: [[mid]]the outer and inner terms give d x plus e x, so d plus e must equal b. [[last]]The last terms give d times e, so d times e must equal c. [[rule]]To factor x squared plus b x plus c, look for two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.
beats.table: Factor x squared plus eight x plus fifteen. [[list]]List the factor pairs of fifteen: one and fifteen, three and five. [[sums]]Check each sum: one plus fifteen is sixteen, [[hit]]three plus five is eight. That's b. [[ans]]So the answer is x plus three, times x plus five. [[order]]The order of the two factors doesn't matter.
beats.signs: Signs tell you where to look. [[pp]]If c is positive and b is positive, both numbers are positive. [[nn]]If c is positive but b is negative, both numbers are negative: x squared minus ten x plus twenty-one is x minus three, times x minus seven. [[mix]]If c is negative, the numbers have opposite signs. [[ex]]For x squared plus two x minus thirty-five, the pair is negative five and seven: [[ans]]x minus five, times x plus seven.
beats.careful: Be careful which number gets the minus sign. [[a]]x plus seven, times x minus five, gives plus two x. [[b]]x minus seven, times x plus five, gives minus two x. [[diff]]They're different trinomials, so check the middle term every time.
beats.none: Not every trinomial can be factored this way. [[ex]]Take x squared plus five x plus three. [[pairs]]The only integer pairs that multiply to three are one and three, and negative one and negative three. [[sums]]Their sums are four and negative four, never five. [[nf]]So it doesn't factor into binomials with integers.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]To factor x squared plus b x plus c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. [[w2]]The signs of b and c tell you the signs of the two numbers. [[w3]]Check the middle term by multiplying back. [[w4]]If no pair works, the trinomial can't be factored with integers. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. More practice with signs.
beats.finish: Great work. That's the end of chapter fifty-four, factoring trinomials.
